# Rubick

> A free desktop Kubernetes client (macOS, Windows, Linux) that tries not to lie to you: it derives pod status the way kubectl does instead of trusting .status.phase, reads the endpoints the cluster actually publishes, and draws the Ingress-to-pod traffic chain naming the exact link that broke. GPL-3.0-or-later, no account, no telemetry. Built with Tauri and Rust.

Key facts: reads your kubeconfig like Lens, k9s or Headlamp; warns who will undo a change (HPA, Argo CD, Flux) before obeying; integrates with Traefik, ingress-nginx, Istio, cert-manager, Argo CD, Flux, Prometheus, Loki, GKE, EKS and AKS; requires Kubernetes 1.21+.

## Pages

- [Home](https://rubick.tech/): what Rubick shows that dashboards miss, and downloads for every platform
- [Lie 1, "Running"](https://rubick.tech/lies/running): a crashlooping pod that reports phase Running, and how Rubick reads it
- [Lie 2, "All green"](https://rubick.tech/lies/all-green): a Service with a mistyped port name that publishes nothing
- [Lie 3, "No route"](https://rubick.tech/lies/no-route): an Ingress rule to a Service that does not exist
- [Reproduce the three lies](https://rubick.tech/lies.yaml): a manifest for any throwaway cluster
- [Rubick vs Lens](https://rubick.tech/vs/lens): an honest comparison with Lens by Mirantis
- [Rubick vs k9s](https://rubick.tech/vs/k9s): an honest comparison with the k9s terminal UI
- [Rubick vs Headlamp](https://rubick.tech/vs/headlamp): an honest comparison with the Headlamp web UI
